text: Four kyu, forty years, one park bench.
Corner, side, centre. Learn it in that order and you'll save yourself a decade.
You've been watching Pip, then. He's been trying the same thing since he got here and it has never once worked, and I have never once managed to explain why.
Sit down. I'll show you the version that does work, and the ten seconds of counting that tells you which one you've got.
Read it to the end. That's it. That's the whole of what I know that Pip doesn't.
Corner, side, centre, and read your ladders. Forty years and I could have had it on a postcard.
I'll be on this bench. I am always on this bench.
Right. Sit down. You've had the theory and the theory is worthless.
Four kyu, forty years, one park bench. I'm not going to fight you -- I'm going to out-count you, and you'll not notice until it's done.
Doesn't go on anybody's card. Nothing in this park does.

exit.intro: Stone table, four kyu, no card. He plays first and does not ask.

text: Again. You've got the taste for it now.
Same terms. Nothing written down, nothing owed.

exit.intro: The same bench. He has already set the bowls out.

text: Forty years and the answer's still the same: somebody comes along who counts faster. Good. Go on then.
Territory, see. You were busy having a lovely time in the middle and I was busy owning the edges.
Proverb for you: the corner is gold, the side is silver, the centre is grass. Doesn't always apply. Applied there.
